# Native Codex fixtures

The seven synthetic scenarios cover text, result before idle, resume, interrupt, approval withdrawal,
grouped questions, and quota/token updates. They use the installed 0.162.1 generated schema.

`probe-session`, `probe-interrupted-start`, and `probe-restart` were recorded from the installed
Windows Codex 0.162.1 executable on 2026-10-26 using `aura-cli probe codex`. The free probe passed
20 checks with zero failures and six explicit skips. No prompt or steer was sent. These recordings
prove controls and process lifecycle only; they do not prove prompted resume or turn settings.

Curation replaced home, host, session and spawn identities. Account usage and plan values,
installation identity, configured MCP server names and incidental stderr were sanitized. Native
request/response ordering and shapes remain intact. Model metadata is the public advertised catalog.
Generated goldens are reviewed outputs of the actual Rust driver running against fake pipes.

## Derived session-controls handshake

The active fixtures were migrated on 2026-11-02 for the controls introduced in `9607df94`.
They are derived replay inputs, not new native recordings. The four curated captured inputs are
preserved byte-for-byte under `originals/*.jsonl.original`; their extension keeps them out of the
active replay scan. Their original event stream, request IDs, timestamps, usage and tool outcomes
remain in the derived input.

`adapt-controls.mjs` makes only these changes:

- Mark the input as derived and enable `initialize.capabilities.experimentalApi`.
- Before the first usage-limit read, expect `collaborationMode/list`; after that outgoing read,
  supply a synthetic empty catalog. The unique recorded ID `aura-replay-collaboration` uses the
  harness's existing ID correlation, so recorded request/response IDs never need renumbering.
- Keep interrupted startup without a collaboration exchange when it never reached Ready.

The empty catalog is synthetic compatibility input, not evidence of the current native CLI's
advertised modes. It does not claim the original CLI advertised Plan. Native Plan behavior has
separate driver tests. The stable 0.162.1 schema excludes this experimental list method, so the
schema fixture test validates these two synthetic frames exactly and continues validating all
original frames against the unchanged stable bundle.

Run `node crates/aura-drivers/tests/fixtures/codex/adapt-controls.mjs` from the repository root to
verify every derived input and the unchanged captured fields. `--write` reconstructs the derived
inputs. Regenerate goldens only after replay transport matches; `AURA_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` deliberately
refuses to bless a transport mismatch. The refreshed ACP/Claude goldens also retain the Access and
Workflow options introduced in `9607df94`, whose earlier expected outputs had not been updated.

The 2026-11-02 golden review compared all 48 changed expected outputs with their prior versions.
Every non-option event, reply and exit stayed identical. After removing the added Access/Workflow
entries and repeated unchanged option snapshots, the entire ordered event stream also stayed
identical, including every model and effort choice. Thirty-four goldens only gained the new
controls. Twelve Codex goldens gained one options snapshot after the derived catalog exchange;
Claude `recorded-basic` gained the controls snapshot after an autonomy confirmation in `9607df94`;
`recorded-thinking` lost a repeated snapshot after model alias reconciliation in `d42756a0`.
Neither changes a choice.
No production code or replay contract was relaxed.

Local validation passed the normal replay test over all 94 fixtures, its scenario/privacy checks,
all three Codex schema tests, and targeted replay/schema Clippy with warnings denied. The migration
check passed for all 13 inputs, and the four archived recordings matched their pre-migration Git
blobs byte-for-byte. This is replay evidence, not another live-agent probe.

The interrupted-start recording intentionally closes before Ready. Its recorded shutdown command
and closed exit distinguish cancellation from startup failure. The replay selects the recorded
client version in `initialize` and still compares complete native request payloads.

`recorded-basic` captures one visible `Reply with exactly: ok` turn on GPT-6-Luna with low effort.
The installed CLI streamed `ok`, reported native per-turn usage and shut down normally. It has the
same personal metadata curation as the free recordings. Its first golden was generated by the
existing checkpoint's replay CLI. At capture time, Windows Application Control refused the newly
built local test executables with error 4551. CI checkpoint `e2416e7`
subsequently passed this replay and the generated schema checks on Linux and Windows.

`approval-available-decisions` is synthetic, using the restricted menu observed in the subsequent
real permission scenario. Only `accept` and `cancel` are exposed; the unsupported persistent policy
amendment is omitted. Direct attempts to send unadvertised session approval or decline are ignored.
Its expected golden was derived from `approval-withdrawal` with the two approval menus narrowed,
then verified by the actual Rust driver on Linux and Windows CI at `e2416e7`.
The stable schema permits the native `availableDecisions` extension.

The real permission smoke stopped after native allow-once failed before process creation with
`helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`. Denial left the file absent, and allow-once also
left it absent. The original owned logs remain in ignored task scratch. The obsolete decline choice
in that recording is intentionally not presented as a passing replay of the corrected menu.
